# Git Commit & Contributor Subsystem API Specification (`git_ast`)

Authoritative architectural specification and relational staging reference for `parser/git_ast/`
([git_commit_parser.py](parser/git_ast/git_commit_parser.py), [git_types.py](parser/git_ast/git_types.py)).
Designed as an exhaustive reference for AI agents extending, maintaining, or querying kernel commit histories,
multi-person trailer contributions, merge lineages, and commit-to-code tag bridges.

## 1. High-Level Architecture & Pipeline Flow

The Git Commit subsystem operates in a coordinated two-phase ingestion architecture:
1. **Phase 1 (Step 1: `ingest_git_dag()` in `pipeline/git_ingest.py`)**: Traverses the Git DAG, registering commits (`m_commit` Table 21), parent linkages (`m_commit_parent` Table 33), contributor identities (`m_maintainer_person` Table 15), and contributor roles (`m_bridge_commit_person` Table 22) along with repository references (`m_git_ref` Table 32).
2. **Phase 2 (Step 6.5: `processing_git_commits()` in `pipeline/commits.py`)**: Executes streaming diff log analysis (`git log -p -U0`), extracts modified files (`m_commit_file` Table 23), bridges diff hunks to AST occurrence tags (`m_bridge_commit_tag` Table 24), extracts commit relations (`m_commit_relation` Table 63), and extracts message trailers (`m_commit_link` Table 64).

```
==================================================================================================
GIT COMMIT & MULTI-CONTRIBUTOR PARSING PIPELINE (TWO-PHASE INGESTION)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Kernel Git Repository (linux/)
  │
  ├─► [PHASE 1: Step 1 (ingest_git_dag in pipeline/git_ingest.py)]
  │   ├── Traverses commit DAG (git rev-list / git log)
  │   ├── Ingests m_commit (Table 21) & m_commit_parent (Table 33)
  │   ├── Registers author/committer identities into m_maintainer_person (Table 15)
  │   ├── Records author & trailer roles into m_bridge_commit_person (Table 22)
  │   └── Binds branch/tag refs into m_git_ref (Table 32)
  │
  └─► [PHASE 2: Step 6.5 (processing_git_commits in pipeline/commits.py)]
      ├── Streaming Delimiter-Delimited Git Log Execution:
      │   └── git log <range> -p -U0 --format="%x1e%H%x1f%an%x1f%ae%x1f%at%x1f%cn%x1f%ce%x1f%ct%x1f%s%x1f%B%x1d"
      ├── Modified Files: m_commit_file (Table 23) (excludes merges)
      ├── Code Occurrence Tag Bridge: m_bridge_commit_tag (Table 24)
      ├── Commit Relations: m_commit_relation (Table 63: Fixes:, reverts, backports, Cc: stable)
      └── Trailer Message-IDs: m_commit_link (Table 64: Link:, Message-Id: trailers)
==================================================================================================
```

## 2. Relational Schema Mapping (Tables 15, 21–24, 30–33, 63–64)

`git_ast` populates core relational tables tracking contributor identities (`m_maintainer_person` 15), commit metadata (`m_commit` 21), contributors (`m_bridge_commit_person` 22), affected files (`m_commit_file` 23), code tags (`m_bridge_commit_tag` 24), multi-remote networks (`m_git_network` 30, `m_repository` 31, `m_git_ref` 32), DAG parent topology (`m_commit_parent` 33), and commit relations/mail links (`m_commit_relation` 63, `m_commit_link` 64). See `core/API.md` §4 for the authoritative column and primary-key schema registry.

### 2.0. Merge Commits Stage No File Rows

Commit file rows and diff hunks both come from one `git log -p -U0` stream
(`parse_version_commits_with_hunks`). **`git log -p` prints no diff for a commit with more than one parent**,
so a merge commit reaches `parse_commit_log_with_hunks` with an empty patch part and is staged with `files =
[]` — no `m_commit_file` rows and no `m_bridge_commit_tag` rows, even when the merge resolved a conflict
itself (an "evil merge", e.g. `1f922d0770` in `v3.0`, which changes `arch/sparc/include/asm/ptrace.h`).

This is deliberate: `--diff-merges=first-parent` would make each merge repeat the whole delta of the branch it
merges, which on the full history up to `v3.0` grows the log stream from ~53 MB to ~734 MB per release range
and would re-attribute every merged hunk to the merge commit as well. A merge's first-parent delta is instead
resolved from Git **on demand** by the webapp
(`webapp/backend/services/git_service.py:_fill_missing_commit_files`, `webapp/API.md`
§`/api/commits/{v}/detail/{id}`), which is what keeps the *Modified Files* list in agreement with the commit's
rendered diff.

### 2.1. Staging Example

```python
# 1. Register Commit (Phase 1: Step 1)
commit_row = m_commit.set(
    None,            # commit_id (AUTO_INCREMENT)
    network_id,      # network_id (FK -> m_git_network)
    commit_hash,     # 20-byte binary git commit SHA (bytes)
    author_id,       # FK -> m_maintainer_person.person_id (Table 15)
    author_date,     # Unix epoch timestamp
    committer_id,    # FK -> m_maintainer_person.person_id (Table 15)
    committer_date,  # Unix epoch timestamp
    subject[:500],   # Commit subject line
    body,            # Full commit message
)
commit_id = commit_row[2][0]

# 2. Stage Contributor Roles (Phase 1: Step 1)
m_bridge_commit_person.set(commit_id, author_id, CommitRole.AUTHOR, 0)
m_bridge_commit_person.set(commit_id, committer_id, CommitRole.COMMITTER, 1)
for priority, (person_id, role) in enumerate(trailers):
    m_bridge_commit_person.set(commit_id, person_id, role, priority + 2)

# 3. Stage Modified Files & Tags (Phase 2: Step 6.5)
for fnid, blob_id, old_fnid, old_blob_id, change_type in modified_files:
    m_commit_file.set(commit_id, fnid, blob_id, old_fnid, old_blob_id, change_type)

for blob_id, tag_id in affected_tags:
    m_bridge_commit_tag.set(commit_id, blob_id, tag_id)

# 4. Stage Commit Relations & Trailer Links (Phase 2: Step 6.5)
for kind, idx, target_hash, target_prefix, note in relations:
    m_commit_relation.set(commit_id, kind, idx, target_hash, target_prefix, note)

for mid in message_ids:
    m_commit_link.set(commit_id, mid)
```

## 3. Contributor Taxonomy & Structured Trailers

Kernel commits frequently feature contributions from multiple developers beyond the git commit author and
committer. `git_commit_parser.py` parses structured trailers defined in `git_types.py:CommitRole`:

| Role Constant | `CommitRole` Value | Trailer Prefix in Commit Message |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| `CommitRole.AUTHOR` | 1 | Git Author header (`Author: Name <email>`) |
| `CommitRole.COMMITTER` | 2 | Git Committer header (`Commit: Name <email>`) |
| `CommitRole.CO_DEVELOPED_BY` | 3 | `Co-developed-by: Name <email>` |
| `CommitRole.SIGNED_OFF_BY` | 4 | `Signed-off-by: Name <email>` |
| `CommitRole.REVIEWED_BY` | 5 | `Reviewed-by: Name <email>` |
| `CommitRole.ACKED_BY` | 6 | `Acked-by: Name <email>` |
| `CommitRole.TESTED_BY` | 7 | `Tested-by: Name <email>` |
| `CommitRole.REPORTED_BY` | 8 | `Reported-by: Name <email>` |
| `CommitRole.SUGGESTED_BY` | 9 | `Suggested-by: Name <email>` |
| `CommitRole.MERGED_BY` | 10 | Pull request merger (`merged-by` / `merger`) |
| `CommitRole.REQUESTED_BY` | 11 | Pull request requester (`requested-by` / `Pull from:`) |
| `CommitRole.OTHER` | 12 | Unclassified trailer tag |

Contributors are sanitized and stored in `m_maintainer_person` (Table 15), linking maintainer identities with
git author and trailer histories across releases.

**Reading a trailer** (`iter_trailers(message)` → `(prefix, name, email)`): the one reading of
`TRAILER_PATTERN`'s groups, used by both commit parsers here, the release statistics step (§7) and the
webapp's release passes (`webapp/backend/services/release_service.py`). The email is the `<…>` part, else a
bare address (`Reported-by: syzbot+…@syzkaller.appspotmail.com`); a trailer without a name takes its address
as the name. The name group is optional and lazy (`(?:…)??`): taken greedily, it captured the first character
of a bare address (`s` + `yzbot+…@…`).

**Identities** (`parser/git_ast/identity.py`, pure): `person_key(name, email)` is the `m_maintainer_person`
key every writer uses (`main._person_key()` delegates to it); `clean_name()` / `identity_key()` group a
developer's `(name, email)` aliases by folded name — the Developers directory's rule (`webapp/API_ENDPOINTS.md` §4.5),
imported by `webapp/backend/services/maintainer_service.py`. `build_identity_index(personas)` (with
`merge_emails()`) adds the name-less rule (a name-less alias joins the named identity owning its address; the
identity using it on most personas, then the largest, wins), and `refresh_person_identities(cnx)`, the
module's only I/O, stores the result in `m_person_identity` (`core/API.md` §4 row 59).

## 4. Diff Hunk Extraction & Line Coordinate Tag Bridging

`git_ast` bridges commits to AST code occurrence tags (`m_tag`) using diff coordinate spatial indexing:

### 4.1. Hunk Interval Representation (`CommitDiffHunk`)
- `git log -p -U0` gives each hunk as `@@ -old_start,old_count +new_start,new_count @@`, in that commit's own
  version of the file.
- Tags carry the lines of the range's newest version, so `parse_commit_log_with_hunks()` (and
  `extract_file_hunks()`) move every hunk there with `_HeadLineMapper`: commits arrive newest first, and a
  commit's range is mapped through the hunks of every newer commit that touched the file (`_map_line()`: lines
  after a hunk shift by its size change, a replaced line maps into the replacement). Renames carry the chain
  to the old name; a file (re)created by a newer commit ends it. `file_hunks_map` is keyed by the newest path.
- Patch headers are only read between `diff --git` and the first hunk (patch content can never be taken for
  `--- /dev/null` etc.); `index`, `rename from/to` and `new/deleted file mode` lines give each file's change
  type, old path and blobs (`GitCommit.file_blobs`).

### 4.2. Tag Correlation (`map_tags_to_commits`)
- For each tag `(tag_id, fid, line_s, line_e)` of a changed file, the commits whose hunks overlap its lines
  (`_HunkIndex` beyond 8 hunks, a scan below) are staged into `m_bridge_commit_tag(commit_id, blob_id,
  tag_id)`.
- A tag no hunk touches (unchanged code of a changed file, recycled tags) is linked to no commit.
- This enables web applications and static analysis tools to query all commits that modified a specific
  function, struct, or macro across kernel versions in $O(1)$ time.

## 5. Multi-Tree DAG Ingestion & Cross-Tree Content Deduplication

### 5.1. Root Commit Discovery & Git Network Resolution (`resolve_git_network_and_repo`)
When indexing multiple Git repositories (e.g., mainline `torvalds/linux` alongside subsystem trees like
`linux-next`), the parser discovers the repository's root commit via:
```bash
git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD
```
For Linux, this resolves to root commit `1da177e4c3f41524e886b7f1b8a0c1fc7321cac2` ("Linux-2.6.12-rc2").
- Trees that share the identical root commit hash are registered under the same `m_git_network` record.
- Distinct repositories pointing to that network are tracked individually in `m_repository(repo_id,
  network_id, name, git_url, default_branch)`.
- A new network belongs to the `m_project` of the repository's configured `project` slug (`linux`
  "Linux Kernel", `man-pages` "Linux man-pages" for the man-pages tree rooted at
  `fea681dafb1363a154b7fc6d59baa83d2a9ebc5c`) and is named `<slug>-network` (`core/API.md` §7.1.1).

### 5.2. Complete Git DAG Ingestion (`ingest_git_dag`)
The Git commit DAG is ingested upfront before file AST parsing:
- **Topology**: Traverses full commit lineages, staging parents into `m_commit_parent(commit_id,
  parent_commit_id, parent_idx)`.
- **References**: Registers tags and branches into `m_git_ref(ref_id, repo_id, ref_type, ref_name, commit_id,
  ...)`.
- **Commit relations**: the new commits' messages are parsed into `m_commit_relation` / `m_commit_link` in the
  same bulk insert (§8).
- **Backward Compatibility**: `gp.VID` is anchored to the target Git reference's `head_commit_id`, ensuring
  downstream relational tables seamlessly align with `m_bridge_checkpoint` and `m_v_main`.

### 5.3. Content-Addressable Blob Deduplication Across Trees
Git trees are enumerated via `git ls-tree -r {version}` into 20-byte SHA-1 digests.
- Before queuing files for parallel worker AST parsing, existing blobs in `m_file_blob` with matching
  `(blob_hash, ftype)` and valid `m_bridge_tag` records are linked directly into `m_bridge_checkpoint` and
  `m_commit_file`.
- Deduplicated files bypass Phase 1 worker queues entirely, eliminating redundant AST extraction across
  branches or trees sharing identical source files.

## 6. Performance Invariants & Architectural Rules

1. **Streaming Delimited Ingestion**:
   - Uses binary control characters (`RECORD_SEP`, `FIELD_SEP`, `BODY_END_SEP`) rather than custom regex or
     multiline string splits, preventing catastrophic backtracking and parsing 100,000+ kernel commits in
     seconds.
   - Record chunks are trimmed with `strip(" \t\r\n")`, never bare `strip()`: Python treats `\x1c`–`\x1f` as
     whitespace, and a bare strip removes the trailing `BODY_END_SEP` of merge commits (which have no
     `--name-status` file list), silently dropping every merge and every DAG edge through it.
2. **Subprocess Buffer Protection**:
   - `_run_git()` caps output buffer at `max_output_bytes = 50MB` with explicit process timeouts (120s) by
     default; callers may raise both (e.g. `parse_version_commits()` allows 4 GiB / 1800 s for whole-history
     ranges). Output past `max_output_bytes` is cut mid-record, so the cap logs a warning when it truncates,
     and a timeout logs the whole command (`--format=<spec>` elided) with the deadline it exceeded — not just
     `git -C <repo> log`.
   - `parse_version_commits(old_rev, new_rev, limit=None, with_files=True)`: Without `old_rev` the complete
     history up to `new_rev` is returned (no implicit cap), so the commit DAG reaches the root commit; `limit`
     bounds the count. `with_files=False` omits `--name-status` for DAG-only ingestion (≈9 s for the 255k
     commits up to v3.0).
   - `count_commits(revision_arg)`: `git rev-list --count` walks the DAG without reading a blob, sizing even a
     1.5M-commit range in ~10 s (-1 when git cannot report it).
   - **Diff-stream commit caps** (`parse_version_commits_with_hunks()`): `git log -p -U0` streams every
     changed line of every commit in the range (~1,800 commits/s, ~1.3 KB/commit), so a wide range is
     gigabytes and tens of minutes. With no explicit `limit` the newest commits only are streamed:
     `INITIAL_HUNK_COMMIT_CAP = 1000` without `old_rev` (whole history), and `RANGE_HUNK_COMMIT_CAP = 20000`
     for `old_rev..new_rev`, applied after `count_commits()` sizes the range (or when it cannot). The
     subprocess timeout scales with the commit budget (`budget / 100`, floor 300 s, ceiling 3600 s) and the
     buffer is 1 GiB. Commits past the cap keep the `m_commit`/`m_commit_parent`/`m_bridge_commit_person` rows
     `ingest_git_dag()` already staged; additionally, `parse_version_commits_with_hunks()` issues a fast `git
     log --name-status` query for older commits beyond the hunk cap to preserve file edges (`m_commit_file`),
     and the cap logs which range it bounded. Without the cap a branch tip far from the prior release (e.g.
     `v2.6.12-rc2..assoc-array-fixes`, 1,485,104 commits) hit the subprocess timeout and returned nothing,
     dropping file and tag rows for the whole version; `main.py --limit N` (`gp.commit_limit`) overrides the
     caps, bounding both the DAG ingest and the diff stream.
3. **Interval Index Queries**:
   - Spatial hunk-to-tag correlation (`map_tags_to_commits`, more than 8 hunks) uses `_HunkIndex`: hunks
     sorted by start line with a max-end segment tree, returning the hunks overlapping a tag's line range in
     $O(\log H + \text{matches})$ (in hunk start order) instead of scanning every hunk that starts before the
     tag ends.
4. **Bulk Staging & Cache Bypass**:
   - Commit batches are staged with TableEngine secondary in-memory caching disabled
     (`update_in_mem_indexes=False`) to avoid maintaining hundreds of thousands of ephemeral commit indexes in
     RAM.
5. **Commit DAG Parent Linking**:
   - `git log` lists children before parents. `ingest_git_dag()` registers the range in bulk
     (`_ingest_commit_range()`): existing commits are looked up by hash in chunks of 1,000, persons are loaded
     once, and new persons, commits (ids assigned oldest-first), parents and contributors are inserted with
     multi-row statements instead of several round trips and transaction commits per commit. Persons are
     identified by `(name, email)` (`_person_key()`), the same key the TableEngine uses for
     `m_maintainer_person`. The resulting hash -> id map is kept on `gp.commit_ids_by_hash`;
     `processing_git_commits()` reuses it (looking any other hash, including out-of-range parents, up in one
     batch) and only creates persons for commits not yet registered. It defers `m_commit_parent` rows until
     every commit of the range has an id.
   - Files reused by Step 4.5's blob deduplication (`gp.deduped_paths`) are not parsed:
     `processing_git_commits()` loads their tags from `m_bridge_tag` (`_load_blob_tags()`) and maps them to
     the range's commits like parsed files.
   - `main.py --limit N` bounds the commits `ingest_git_dag()` records per version range (default: all).
6. **Dynamic Repository Routing**:
   - Multi-tree parsing dynamically routes git subprocess invocations to the active repository directory via
     `MF.set_repo_dir(repo_dir)`, maintaining independent Git repository context across diverse tree
     checkouts.
7. **Binary vs Hexadecimal Commit Hash Formatting**:
   - Relational tables store commit hashes in compact 20-byte `BINARY(20)` format. Public APIs, services, and
     webapp endpoints must format binary digests as 40-character lowercase hexadecimal strings
     (`format_commit_hash(val)`: `bytes(val).hex()`) and use `UNHEX(%s)` for SQL queries.

## 7. Release Statistics & Release Order (`release_stats.py`, `release_order.py`)

- **Release order** (`release_order.py`, pure, shared with the webapp's release index, `webapp/API.md` §2.17):
  release tags of any project, in two schemes, each tag carrying its **family** (`parse_tag()["family"]`,
  `family_of()`):
  - **Kernel scheme** (family `""`, `KERNEL_FAMILY`): `vX.Y[.Z][-rcN|-preN]` and bare `X.Y[.Z]`, with v2.6.x
    stable updates as the fourth number (series `(2, 6, x)`), `(X, Y, 0)` series from v3.0 on, and daily
    `next-YYYYMMDD` tags (series `(NEXT_SERIES, year, month)`, kind `next`).
  - **Prefixed scheme** (family = the prefix): `<prefix>X.Y[.Z][-rcN|-preN]` (`PREFIXED_TAG_RE`: the prefix
    starts with a letter and holds no dot, `v` alone being the kernel scheme), e.g. `man-pages-6.9.1`,
    `foo-1.2.3`, `release_2.0-rc1`. The series is `(PREFIXED_SERIES, prefix, X, Y)` compared as numbers
    (`man-pages-6.04` and `man-pages-6.4` name the same series), Z the point release (kind `stable`); a
    release candidate of a point release is not a release.
  - `release_tag_names(names)`: the release tags of a repository — the kernel scheme's when any name uses it
    (prefixed names in a kernel tree, such as `for-linus-6.1` pull-request tags, are not releases), else every
    prefixed release (each prefix its own family).
  - `release_key()` (`v3.0 < v3.0.1 < v3.1-rc1 < v3.1 < v3.1.1`, `foo-1.9 < foo-1.10-rc1 < foo-1.10 <
    foo-1.10.1`; kernel tags before prefixed ones, prefixes alphabetically), `previous_in()` (within the tag's
    family), `final_of()` (a prefixed release candidate leads to the final tag of its series whatever its
    spelling: `man-pages-6.0-rc1` → `man-pages-6.00`), `series_name()` (a name parsing back to the series:
    `v3.1`, `v2.6.39`, `man-pages-6.4`), and `release_ranges(tags)` — every release tag with its segment base
    (previous tag of its chain: the mainline of its family with release candidates, or its stable series) and
    its report range base (`previous_in()`), in one linear pass; every family has chains of its own.
- **Release statistics** (`release_stats.py`): summarizes every release tag into `m_release_segment`,
  `m_release_person`, `m_person_first_release` (`core/API.md` §4, §10): one `git log` per segment, merges
  included (`%H`/`%P` with the message; `summarize_records()` counts a record with two or more parents as a
  merge and skips it for commits and people), read with `iter_trailers()`, plus `git diff --shortstat` over
  the report range; every commit of the segment also gets its `m_commit_release` row (`FORMAT = 2`);
  incremental per tag. Release tags are `release_order.release_tag_names()` of the repository's commit-pointing
  tags, so every project (the Linux kernel, the man-pages, any `<prefix>X.Y` scheme) is summarized.
  `main.processing_release_stats()` runs it at the start and end of every run, whatever the project; `python3
  main.py --release-stats` alone.

## 8. Commit Relations (`commit_relations.py`)

What a commit message says about other commits and mail, parsed by pure functions shared with the webapp's
SQLite relation index (`webapp/backend/services/commit_relations.py` re-exports them):

| Kind | Message text | Stored |
|---|---|---|
| 1 `KIND_FIXES` | `Fixes: <8-40 hex> ("subject")` | target, quoted subject in `note` |
| 2 `KIND_REVERTS` | `This reverts commit <hex>.` | target |
| 3 `KIND_UPSTREAM` | `commit <hex> upstream.`, `[ Upstream commit <hex> ]`, `(cherry picked from commit <hex>)` | target (the commit this one backports; itself excluded) |
| 4 `KIND_STABLE_CC` | `Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # <annotation>` | annotation in `note` (identical ones once) |
| links | `Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/<mid>` (also lkml, patch.msgid.link, marc), `Message-Id: <mid>` | `normalize_mid()`: unbracketed, URL-decoded, lower-case |

- `parse_relations(text)`: the relations of one message; `relation_rows(message, own_sha)`: `([(kind, idx,
  prefix, note)], [mid])`, `idx` the order per kind; `table_rows(commit_id, rels, links, resolved)`: the
  `m_commit_relation` / `m_commit_link` rows (`core/API.md` §4 rows 63-64), `target_hash` zero for a prefix
  that names no commit or several.
- `resolve_prefixes(repo, prefixes)`: `{prefix: sha}` with one `git cat-file --batch-check`
  (`<prefix>^{commit}`); ambiguous and missing prefixes get no answer. Used for the relation targets (once per
  ingested range, once per backfill chunk) and the CVE commit hashes (`core/API.md` §9).
- Writers: `main._ingest_commit_range()` (Step 1, with the commits), `main.stage_commit_relations()` (Step
  6.5, commits it inserts itself), `core/backfills.backfill_commit_relations()`
  (`--backfill-commit-relations`, `core/API.md` §12).
